part.name: Double-sided scissor lift platform assembly
part.description: A compact elevating platform comprising two rectangular slotted platform blocks, paired crossed scissor-link plates on both lateral sides, four platform pivot/guide pins, and two central crossover pins. The elongated slots permit one end of each scissor mechanism to translate while the opposite end pivots about a fixed mounting point.
part.symmetry_note: The assembly is approximately symmetric about its longitudinal mid-plane and approximately symmetric between the lower and upper platforms. The scissor-link geometry is repeated on the positive-z and negative-z sides, with link layers axially offset to allow crossover without interference.

Section.name: Lower platform block
Section.function intent: Provides the lower mounting foundation, carries applied reaction loads, fixes one scissor endpoint, and guides the opposite endpoint along a horizontal slot.
Section.physical behavior: The thick prismatic block resists bending and distributes concentrated pin reactions over a broad section. The fixed bore constrains translation of one endpoint, while the elongated slot permits controlled sliding of the other endpoint during scissor opening and closing.
Section.geometry: A 100 mm long, 45 mm deep, 12 mm thick rectangular block with lightly rounded external edges. One end region contains a straight obround through-slot approximately 25 mm long with semicircular ends, and the opposite end contains a circular through-bore for a fixed pivot pin.
Section.location: Lower member of the assembly at the low-y side of the STEP coordinate system.

Section.name: Upper platform block
Section.function intent: Forms the moving load-support surface and receives the upper endpoints of both scissor mechanisms, with one fixed pivot and one sliding pivot on each lateral side.
Section.physical behavior: The broad prismatic body spreads payload across the scissor supports. Pin loads enter through the fixed bore and guide-slot walls; the slot permits the required horizontal endpoint displacement while the platform rises or lowers.
Section.geometry: A second 100 mm long, 45 mm deep, 12 mm thick rectangular block matching the lower platform. It contains an elongated obround guide slot toward one end and a circular fixed-pivot bore toward the other.
Section.location: Upper member of the assembly at the high-y side of the STEP coordinate system.

Section.name: Positive-z scissor-link pair
Section.function intent: Connects the lower and upper platforms on one lateral side, synchronizes their separation, and converts horizontal endpoint travel into vertical platform movement.
Section.physical behavior: Each slender link primarily carries axial tension or compression with secondary bending near its pivot bosses. The circular bosses spread bearing stress around the pin bores. Axial offset between the two link plates provides crossover clearance while the central pin constrains relative translation but permits rotation.
Section.geometry: Two disconnected, thin, diagonal plates at positive z. Each plate spans between diagonally opposite platform pivots and has enlarged circular bosses at both endpoints and at the central crossing. The two plates occupy adjacent z layers.
Section.location: Positive-z lateral side of the assembly, visible predominantly in the front view.

Section.name: Negative-z scissor-link pair
Section.function intent: Provides the second lateral scissor mechanism, sharing platform load and stabilizing the platforms against twisting or lateral roll.
Section.physical behavior: The paired links carry axial tension and compression in parallel with the positive-z mechanism. Their lateral separation creates a wide support base that improves torsional stiffness, while pivot bores allow rotation and slotted endpoints permit horizontal travel.
Section.geometry: Two thin crossed diagonal plates at negative z, geometrically matching the positive-z pair. Each has long straight arms, enlarged circular pivot bosses, and through-bores at both endpoints and the central crossover.
Section.location: Negative-z lateral side of the assembly, visible predominantly in the back view.

Section.name: Platform pivot and guide pins
features included: two fixed-pivot interfaces per platform level
two sliding guide interfaces per platform level
Section.function intent: Joins both lateral scissor mechanisms to the platform blocks, keeps corresponding front and rear link endpoints coaxial, and provides either fixed rotation or combined rotation and slot translation.
Section.physical behavior: The pins carry transverse shear and local bearing loads from both link sets. Their cylindrical surfaces rotate in the link bores; pins passing through elongated slots also translate along the slot axis. The pin length ties the two lateral mechanisms together and helps maintain parallel alignment.
Section.geometry: Four slender cylinders spanning nearly the full z width of the assembly at the four platform endpoint locations. Each has planar circular ends and small toroidal edge rounds.
Section.location: At the left and right endpoint pivots of both the lower and upper platforms, spanning from negative z to positive z.

Section.name: Central crossover pins
Section.function intent: Connects each pair of crossed link plates at its midpoint and creates the rotational joint governing scissor opening and closing.
Section.physical behavior: Each short pin carries double-shear and bearing loads between the two overlapping link bosses. It constrains relative in-plane translation while allowing the links to rotate about the shared z-directed axis.
Section.geometry: Two short cylindrical pins, one at each lateral side of the assembly, coaxial with the central bosses of their respective crossed-link pair.
Section.location: At the geometric crossing of the scissor links, with one pin near positive z and one near negative z.
